extractor.note: Whole file grep-counted for the theme's search terms plus 'Wesensschau', 'immutable', 'innate', 'residuum' and 'free variation'. Closely read § 7 (lines 113-156), § 16 (285-292) and the opening of § 8 (157-202).

coverage_note: Covers § 7 (regional concepts and genus-concepts) and § 16 (noema and essence) in full, and the opening paragraphs of § 8 (rational psychology and phenomenology), the densest section in the file. §§ 9-15 and the First Chapter were keyword-scanned only.

units.claim: Regional concepts are said to be derivable a priori not by transcendental deduction but by following an apodictically evident transcendental clue, grasped step by step in seeing.
units.quote: and yet it follows an apodictically evident "transcendental clue," which leads us not to deduce but to find and grasp step by step through our own seeing

units.claim: There must be a priori as many ontologies as there are regional concepts, whether those ontologies turn out rich or meager in content.
units.quote: such that a priori there must be as many ontologies as regional concepts

units.claim: Word-meanings as logical essences are said to be valid only if a corresponding essence, graspable through intuition as a noema, finds faithful expression in the logical concept.
units.quote: if there is a corresponding essence, graspable through intuition as a corresponding noema, that finds its faithful "expression" in the logical concept

units.claim: The essential intuition is said to be able to proceed on the ground of a singular imagination, which suffices to grasp the general essence.
units.quote: The essential intuition can proceed on the ground of a singular imagination. It suffices to grasp the general essence

units.claim: The noema of a thing-intuition is declared not to be and not to contain the essence of the thing, the grasping of the one not being the grasping of the other.
units.quote: is not and does not contain the essence of the thing. The grasping of the one is not the grasping of the other

units.claim: Essential intuition (Erschauung) is reserved as a term for the intuitive grasping of essences, so that the intuition of the noema needs a different terminus.
units.quote: Speaking of "essential intuition" (Erschauung) only for the intuitive grasping of essences, we need a different terminus for the intuition of the noema.

units.claim: The essence round square is said not to exist, while the presupposition of judging so is that round square is a meaning existing in the unity of the noema.
units.quote: The essence "round square" does not exist; but to judge this, the presupposition is that "round square" is a meaning existing in this unity.

units.claim: Judging ontologically about essences rather than phenomenologically about the noema is called an essential change of judgment-posture that oversteps phenomenology into ontology.
units.quote: As soon as we perform the required change of judgment-direction, we have overstepped the domain of phenomenology and entered that of ontology.

units.claim: All phenomenological truths are said to belong to rational psychology, first those relating to the reell essential moments of possible experiences.
units.quote: it is certain in advance that all phenomenological truths belong to rational psychology - first and foremost all those relating to the real (reell) essential moments of possible experiences

absences.expected_because: The section separates the grasping of the noema from the grasping of the ontic essence and hands the essence over to ontology, so it is where a claim about essences as a phenomenological residuum, or as innate or immutable natures, would fall.
absences.note: Bears on gap-007. The commentary's essence-vocabulary is 'essential intuition (Erschauung)' and 'ontic essence'; none of the Cartesian vocabulary appears anywhere in the file.
